paragraphs.text: By this repetition he shows that the least of God's benefits bind us to thanksgiving: but chiefly his mercy, which is principally declared towards his Church.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: This was a common kind of thanksgiving, which the whole people used, when they had received any benefit from God, as in 2Ch 7:6,20:21, meaning that God was not only merciful to their fathers, but also continued the same to their posterity.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: God's merciful providence toward man appears in all his creatures, but chiefly in that he delivered his Church from the clutches of their enemies.
paragraphs.label: c
paragraphs.anchor: brought out Israel from among them

paragraphs.text: In doing such a work as was never done before, nor that any other could do.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: Where for the space of forty years he showed infinite and most strange wonders.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: Declaring by it that no power or authority was so dear to him as the love of his Church.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: In our greatest affliction and slavery when we looked for nothing less than to have had any help.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: Seeing that God provides even for the beasts much more has he care over his.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: Seeing that all ages have had most plain testimonies of God's benefits.
paragraphs.label: i
paragraphs.anchor: O give thanks unto the God
